part_a_s9_and_logits.observed_tensor: As v2 observed_tensor: z_s of checkpoint A computed one beat at a time, to_ncl with L = 1, registry v2 quantize_per_channel then dequantize_per_channel; the attacker input is the dequantized FP32 [C] vector (C = 32 at s9, 5 at s10)
part_a_s9_and_logits.logits_definition: The s10 tensor is the FP32 PyTorch output of the full checkpoint A on the normalized beat (classifier.4, 5 values N, S, V, F, Q), quantized like every other split: the nominal 15 B tensor (5 INT8 + 5 FP16) of table_iii. It stands for every logits vector the edge can compute from z_s with the FP32 reference tail it knows (threat_model.knows: tail weights)
part_a_s9_and_logits.kv260_logits: Not attacked: the KV260 INT8 logits (multiples of 0.125) are another function of z_s; omitting a variant can only leave Pi higher, so every Pi here stays an upper bound. Listed in limitations
part_a_s9_and_logits.golden_check: rho0 z_s9 and z_s10 of the 20 package A golden beats must equal golden/z_s9.npy and golden/z_s10.npy bit for bit (v2 golden_check extended to s9, s10)

attacks.A1: v2 attack_models.A1_decoder s9 and s10, seed 20261030; reported, not part of Pi

part_a_s9_and_logits.architecture: Base: the v2 trial capacity check (s0 mean bacc 0.8256 >= 0.80) decided 'base' for every split; it is not repeated and not revised
part_a_s9_and_logits.reported: Per pair as v2 (Pi, CI95, seed range, per-seed results, session bacc, A1 metrics); Pi(s9) is then also combined with B_composite s9 -> s10 in part b
part_a_s9_and_logits.names: Pi_v3(s9, rho0) after part b; Pi_logits = Pi of B_naive on the s10 tensor (no deeper split exists, so no composite)

reading_declared_before_run.Pi_logits_below_Pi_min: Pi_logits < 0.5: with this metric no offload configuration that keeps the logits computable at the edge (every s < 10 under rho0) can reach Pi_min. Recorded as a property of the problem; Pi_min is NOT lowered
reading_declared_before_run.Pi_logits_at_least_Pi_min: Pi_logits >= 0.5: no such statement; Pi(s < 10) stays what its own measurements give
reading_declared_before_run.Pi_s9_at_least_Pi_min: Pi_v3(s9, rho0) >= 0.5: report to SV1, who reopens the bottleneck question (SV1 2026-11-19 section 3, last part)
reading_declared_before_run.Pi_s9_below_Pi_min: Pi_v3(s9, rho0) < 0.5: the bottleneck route stays closed
reading_declared_before_run.action_set: Pi(s10) of the action set is 1 by construction (SV1 2026-11-19 section 5); Pi_logits never filters s10

part_b_B_composite.applies_to: rho0 (checkpoint A) only: every split shares one model, so the edge that receives z_s holds every op after s. Under rho1 each split is a different checkpoint whose deeper-split attackers do not exist; B_composite is not defined for rho1 in this version and Pi(s, rho1) stays B_naive
part_b_B_composite.argument: The edge that receives the observed tensor u_s at s can compute u_s' for any s' > s and run the attacker trained at s'. So the true Pi(s, rho0) cannot exceed Pi(s', rho0) except through the quantization error at s; the measured order 0.100 -> 0.068 reflects attacker weakness at shallow splits. This is the hypothesis part b measures; the trial value Pi(s0) = 0.183 is not used anywhere

sources_and_targets.pairs: Every (s, s') with s in source_splits, s' in target_splits, s' > s: 21 composite evaluations (6 + 5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1)
sources_and_targets.attackers: s' in {2, 4, 5, 8}: the v2 trial attackers <s'>-rho0-attackers.pt (s0 is never a target); s' in {9, 10}: the part a attackers

computation.input: u_s = the observed tensor at s exactly as v2 observed_tensor (for s0: dequantized INT8 x, the 362 B payload)
computation.ops: frozen ops OPS[CUTS[s]:CUTS[s']] of checkpoint A (week3_sv2_common.CUTS), CPU, week3_sv2_common.configure; batched when s' <= 8, one beat at a time when s' >= 9; s9 sources enter as [N, 32] (to_ncl undone)
computation.quantization: z'_s' -> to_ncl -> quantize_per_channel -> dequantize_per_channel (registry v2), so the attacker sees the same kind of tensor it was trained on; the edge can do this itself
computation.standardization: Mean and std of the attacker-train part of the genuine u_s' (the statistics the s' attacker was trained with), recomputed with v2 attack_models.input_standardization
computation.prediction: Each of the 3 seeds' B attackers of (s', rho0) in eval mode on the standardized composite test tensors, argmax; same device and precision settings as the v2 trial (CUDA RTX 5060, deterministic, TF32 off)
computation.metric: Per seed bacc and Adv on the test part; Adv_composite(s -> s') = mean over the 3 seeds
computation.outputs: Composite test predictions per seed and per (s, s') are saved with the test rows and labels (input of part d)

part_b_B_composite.reproduction_gate: Before any composite number: for every loaded target attacker, its predictions on the genuine u_s' test tensors must equal the saved pred_seed<seed> arrays of the v2 trial npz (s' in {2, 4, 5, 8}) or of part a (s' in {9, 10}) element for element. Any difference stops the run before a composite number exists; the difference is reported to SV1
part_b_B_composite.Pi_v3: Pi_v3(s, rho0) = 1 - max(Adv_naive(s), max over s' of Adv_composite(s -> s')), with Adv_naive(s) read from the v2 trial (s in {0, 2, 4, 5, 8}) or part a (s9). The CI95 is the v2 bootstrap applied to the predictions of the winning variant. Every variant's Adv, Pi, seed range and session bacc are reported
part_b_B_composite.unmeasured_splits: s1, s3, s6, s7 are not evaluated; no Pi is stated for them

reading_declared_before_run.role: Part b does not decide a branch: the no_signal branch is already taken (SV1 2026-11-19 section 3). It replaces the trial ordering with the upper bound the paper may state and tests the composite argument
reading_declared_before_run.argument_holds: Pi_v3(s, rho0) close to min over s' >= s of Pi_naive(s', rho0) at every source: the paper writes that splitting under rho0 does not hide the patient at any measured s, with Pi as an upper bound
reading_declared_before_run.argument_fails: If quantization at s makes a composite clearly weaker than B_naive at s' (Adv_composite well below Adv_naive(s')), report the numbers as they are; Pi_v3 still takes the max over variants and stays an upper bound

part_c_rho2_and_s0_noise_control.status: Specification for SV1's review; runs only after the lock of the reviewed version; at most one week in week 12 (SV1 2026-11-19 section 3; 2026-11-20 item 4)

configurations.R2[alpha]: s2 + rho2: on the device, z_s2 of checkpoint A plus Gaussian noise e[c, l] ~ N(0, (alpha * sigma_c)^2), independent per beat, channel and position, then registry v2 quantization; the edge dequantizes and runs the frozen tail
configurations.C0[alpha]: s0 + noise (control): the normalized beat x plus Gaussian noise N(0, (alpha * sigma_x)^2) per sample, then registry v2 quantization, sent at s0; the edge runs the whole frozen model
configurations.sigma: sigma_c = population std over N and L of channel c of the clean z_s2 of checkpoint A on DS1 train; sigma_x = population std of the normalized x over DS1 train. Computed once and written to a file with its SHA-256 before any noisy evaluation. alpha only parametrizes each configuration; the two configurations are compared at equal macro-F1, never at equal alpha (SV1 2026-11-20 item 3(6))

part_c_rho2_and_s0_noise_control.model: Checkpoint A frozen: no retraining of head or tail (questions_for_SV1 item 1). If SV1 chooses a noise-aware fine-tune, part c is rewritten in a new version before any run
part_c_rho2_and_s0_noise_control.noise_generator: numpy.random.default_rng(numpy.random.SeedSequence([20261120, config_index, alpha_key, part_index, draw])) with config_index 0 = R2, 1 = C0; alpha_key = round(alpha * 1e6); part_index 0 attacker-train, 1 attacker-validation, 2 test, 3 DS1 validation; draws 0, 1, 2 for utility; draw 0 for attacker-validation and test; draws 0-4 for the attacker-train realizations of the adaptive attackers

utility.data: DS1 validation (as NoPeek v2 utility); DS2 never used
utility.metric: Macro-F1 over N, S, V, F (fixed4), argmax over 5 outputs, zero_division 0, from the confusion summed over the 3 noise draws, exact with Fraction; per-draw macro-F1 and accuracy also reported
utility.gate: Passes when macro-F1 >= 19/20 x F1_A = 218290747091/404383914000 (0.5398), the threshold of route R and of rho1

matched_utility_search.targets: t in {0.99, 0.98, 0.97, 0.95} x F1_A; the last target is the gate
matched_utility_search.rule: For each configuration and target t, utility only on the coarse grid; then bisection in log(alpha) between the largest grid alpha with macro-F1 >= t and the next grid alpha, 8 steps; alpha_t = the largest alpha found with macro-F1 >= t. If even 0.05 fails t, alpha_t is searched downward to 0.05/2^8; if no alpha reaches t, the target is reported unreachable. If macro-F1 is not monotone on the grid, the first crossing from small alpha is used and the non-monotone points are reported
matched_utility_search.selection_data: DS1 validation only; selecting alpha on DS1 validation is allowed (DS2 stays closed and unused)
matched_utility_search.privacy_points: Pi is evaluated at alpha_t of each reachable target for each configuration: at most 8 privacy points (4 targets x 2 configurations), at least 4 levels per configuration as SV1 asked

privacy.data: v2 trial data and time split (DS1, N = 22)
privacy.attacker_knowledge: The attacker knows the mechanism, the checkpoint and alpha and sigma (SV1 2026-11-20 item 3(6); roadmap 8.3), and holds labelled clean attacker-side beats of the N patients as in v2

variants.B_naive: Base architecture at the source split (s2 for R2, s0 for C0), trained on one noisy realization (draw 0) of the attacker-train tensors
variants.B_adaptive: Same architecture, trained on the attacker-train beats with the noise regenerated from the known distribution: epoch e uses realization (e - 1) mod 5 of 5 pre-drawn realizations (draws 0-4)
variants.B_composite_adaptive: For each s' in {2, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10} with s' > source: the edge computes u_s' from the noisy observed tensor (part b computation, frozen checkpoint A); a base-architecture attacker at s' is trained on the same pipeline applied to the 5 attacker-train realizations (epoch e uses realization (e - 1) mod 5) and tested on the composite of the noisy test tensors. Standardization statistics from realization 0 of its own attacker-train part

privacy.seeds_and_training: Every variant: 3 seeds 20261030, 20261031, 20261101, v2 training settings (AdamW, early stop on attacker-validation bacc with the fixed draw-0 validation tensors, patience 5, max 50 epochs, TF32 off)
privacy.Pi: Pi(config, alpha) = 1 - max over the variants of the mean-seed Adv (v2 privacy_metric); CI95 by the v2 bootstrap on the winning variant; every variant reported
privacy.A1: A1 at the source split (1 seed, draw-0 noisy tensors); reported, not part of Pi
privacy.variant_count: Per privacy point: 2 + 5 = 7 variants for R2, 2 + 6 = 8 for C0, each with 3 seeds

action_set_rules_declared_before_run.pass: A configuration passes at alpha when Pi(config, alpha) >= 0.5 (point estimate, strongest variant) and macro-F1 >= the gate
action_set_rules_declared_before_run.C0_passes: If C0 passes at some alpha: s0 + noise enters the action set instead of s2 + rho2, whatever R2 gives (SV1 2026-11-20 item 3(6)); report to SV1 at once
action_set_rules_declared_before_run.only_R2_passes: If no C0 alpha passes and R2 passes at some alpha: route R is reached and s2 + rho2 enters the action set for beats that need privacy (ASI direction v2, section 3.3); report to SV1 at once
action_set_rules_declared_before_run.neither: Otherwise: no new action; the matched-F1 table and the (macro-F1, Pi) curves of R2 and C0 are reported as the privacy-utility result of the negative finding
action_set_rules_declared_before_run.comparison: At every reachable target t: Pi(R2, alpha_t) and Pi(C0, alpha_t) with CI95 and per-variant values, side by side at equal macro-F1
action_set_rules_declared_before_run.decision_time: SV1 decides routes R and K at the end of week 13 with these rules (ASI direction v2, section 3.3)

part_c_rho2_and_s0_noise_control.not_measured: E_prot of the noise generation on the nRF52840 (SV1 2026-11-19 section 8); the energy comparison of an admitted configuration belongs to G5 v2

part_d_k_raw_beats.question: How many beats of one patient must the edge see before it re-identifies the patient (SV1 2026-11-20 item 3(3))? Supports the threat-model statement that the leakage budget does not hide identity
part_d_k_raw_beats.inputs: Saved per-beat test predictions only, no training: the v2 trial predictions (read, never edited) and the part a and part b predictions. For each measured s under rho0 the variant that wins Pi_v3(s, rho0); s0 is the primary row

modes.consecutive: Per patient, the test beats in time order cut into non-overlapping blocks of k consecutive beats; a last block shorter than k is dropped
modes.scattered: Per patient, 200 draws of k test beats without replacement, numpy.random.default_rng(numpy.random.SeedSequence([20261120, 4, s, k])), as when a policy offloads only part of the beats

part_d_k_raw_beats.statistic: Majority vote of each seed's predictions in a block or draw (ties: lowest label); bacc = mean over the N patients of the fraction of the patient's blocks or draws voted to the right identity; Adv_k per seed, mean over the 3 seeds; seed range reported
part_d_k_raw_beats.status: Discussion only, never Pi and never a decision rule. The consecutive k = 10 value can differ from the v2 session bacc, which kept the shorter last block

constraints: The 9 pairs of the v2 trial are never rerun or edited; their files are read only and checked against receipt b2861c71
DS2 is not opened by any part of this version; the official DS2 round needs its own authorization (questions_for_SV1 item 4)
Pi_min = 0.5, the Pi formula, the attack models, the data split and the capacity decision are those of v2
Trial numbers stay an early warning and never enter the paper's main numbers
run_order_after_lock: Part a: golden check s9, s10; B_naive and A1 at s9 then s10; report Pi_v3(s9) and Pi_logits the day they exist
Part b: v2 receipt check, reproduction gate, then the 21 composite evaluations; report the Pi_v3 table
Part d: from the saved predictions of the v2 trial and parts a and b; report with the Pi_v3 table
Part c: sigma file first, then the matched-utility search (DS1 validation), then the privacy points; at most one week
limitations: v2 limitations apply (N = 21 official, no sex/age inference, trial on DS1 patients seen in training)

Closed-set re-identification of N patients with attacker train and test from two halves of the same record: identity is confounded with session features (electrodes, posture), so Adv is higher than for cross-session re-identification; MIT-BIH has one session per patient and cannot separate the two

Direction of the bounds: with respect to attacker strength every measured Pi is an upper bound of the in-session Pi; with respect to the session confound the in-session Adv is an upper bound of the cross-session Adv (the in-session Pi a lower bound of the cross-session Pi). The negative result is therefore stated for the in-session closed-set task
The edge already knows which device sends; the threat is linking beats to an identity in another dataset or session, of which the in-session Adv is an upper bound

Leakage budget (SV1 2026-11-20 item 3(3)): Pi measures re-identification, while the budget's asset is the clinical content of each beat, which the A1 reconstruction metrics measure. With the trial numbers both give almost the same per-beat weight (Pi about 0.07, Pearson about 0.99 at every s < 10), but the threat model states which weight the budget uses; since every Pi is an upper bound, 1 - Pi is a lower bound of the per-beat leakage
KV260 INT8 logits are not attacked; B_composite and part a cover rho0 only

rho2 and the s0 control are evaluated with checkpoint A frozen (no noise-aware fine-tune) unless SV1 decides otherwise; Pi for them is an upper bound with respect to stronger adaptive attackers (for example denoising or more noise realizations)
questions_for_SV1: 1. rho2 with checkpoint A frozen, or a noise-aware fine-tune per alpha on DS1 train (selection on DS1 validation)? Frozen fits one week; the fine-tune is closer to Abuadbba 2020 and to the old P2 idea, and it changes the ops the composite attack uses
2. Matched-utility targets {0.99, 0.98, 0.97, 0.95} x F1_A, with alpha found by grid plus bisection on DS1 validation: acceptable?
3. Adaptive attacker with 5 pre-drawn noise realizations of the attacker-train data (cycled over epochs): enough, or more?
4. Should B_composite and the s9/s10 pairs also enter the official DS2 round when it is authorized? Default in this draft: yes, under that round's own authorization
5. Please send the original file of the 2026-11-20 reply: the bound copy is a transcription of the pasted text
